title: QUIZ - 55
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Solving and Graphing an Inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-step inequality and determine its correct graphical representation
questions.question: After solving \( 3a + 7 > 4 \) for a, how should the solution be graphed on a number line?

options.label: A
options.text: A closed circle at -1, shaded to the right.

options.label: B
options.text: A closed circle at -1, shaded to the left.

options.label: C
options.text: An open circle at -1, shaded to the right.

options.label: D
options.text: An open circle at -1, shaded to the left.

questions.explanation: Solving gives a > -1. Since the symbol is \( > \), use an open circle at -1 and shade to the right.
questions.hint: First solve the inequality for the variable, then apply the open/closed circle and shading direction rules.

questions.concept: Shading Direction on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the correct shading direction for an inequality graphed on a number line
questions.question: When graphing \( a \geq 5 \) on a number line, which direction does the shading/arrow point?

options.label: A
options.text: No shading is used, only the boundary point is marked.

options.label: B
options.text: To the right, toward greater values.

options.label: C
options.text: To the left, toward smaller values.

options.label: D
options.text: The shading points in both directions from the boundary.

questions.explanation: Since the inequality is \(a \geq 5\), the solutions extend toward larger values (to the right).
questions.hint: 'Greater than' inequalities shade to the right; 'less than' inequalities shade to the left.

questions.concept: Shading Direction on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the correct shading direction for an inequality graphed on a number line
questions.question: When graphing \( x < 0 \) on a number line, which direction does the shading/arrow point?

options.label: A
options.text: To the left, toward smaller values.

options.label: B
options.text: To the right, toward greater values.

options.label: C
options.text: The shading points in both directions from the boundary.

options.label: D
options.text: No shading is used, only the boundary point is marked.

questions.explanation: Since the inequality is x < 0, the solutions extend toward smaller values (to the left).
questions.hint: 'Greater than' inequalities shade to the right; 'less than' inequalities shade to the left.

questions.concept: Open vs. Closed Circles on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an inequality's graph uses an open or closed circle at the boundary
questions.question: When graphing \( x \geq 8 \) on a number line, what type of circle/dot is used at 8?

options.label: A
options.text: An open circle, because the inequality does not include equality.

options.label: B
options.text: A square marker is used to indicate the boundary.

options.label: C
options.text: No circle is used; only an arrow is drawn.

options.label: D
options.text: A closed (filled) circle, because the inequality includes equality.

questions.explanation: The symbol \( \geq \) includes the boundary value, so a closed (filled) circle is used.
questions.hint: Strict inequalities (> or <) use an open circle; inequalities with 'or equal to' use a closed circle.
